findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:11 — `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError when the query returns no rows. The `embed_category` site setting defaults to `''` and is only stored when an admin sets it, so on most installs there is no matching row, `[0]` is nil, and the migration crashes, blocking all upgrades. The `if category_id == 0` fallback at line 14 is unreachable dead code because the crash happens first, and line 15 has the same unguarded `[0]['value']` pattern.

[High/data] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — Migrated host values are inserted verbatim, without stripping scheme/path the way the model's `before_validation` does. The old setting explicitly supported entries like `http://discourse.org` or `https://example.com/1234`, but `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` compares `lower(host)` to `URI(...).host` (scheme-less, path-less), so those rows will never match and previously working embeds silently break after upgrade. The raw INSERT also bypasses the model's format validation and can insert empty strings (trailing newline in the old setting) and values that fail validation.

[Medium/security] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25 — `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (...) VALUES ('#{h}', ...)"` interpolates the raw site-setting value directly into SQL. A value containing a quote breaks the migration, and it is a SQL injection vector for the (unvalidated) stored setting. Use a parameterized query or ActiveRecord records.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 + app/models/embeddable_host.rb:6 — A request missing `embeddable_host` (or the `host` key) causes an unguarded nil dereference: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` in the controller and `self.host.sub!` in `before_validation` both raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 422 validation error.

[Medium/bug] app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:10-16 — `update` and `destroy` do `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` with no not-found handling; a nonexistent/invalid id passes `nil` into `save_host` (`nil.host =`) or calls `nil.destroy`, raising NoMethodError and returning 500 instead of 404.

[Medium/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 vs :16 — The validation regex permits an optional port (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`), but `record_for_host` matches on `uri.host`, which excludes the port. A host saved as `example.com:3000` can never match a referer from that port, silently breaking embedding for that entry.

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:~194-199 — The new plural branch unconditionally does `obj[pluralize(subType)] = hydrated; delete obj[k];` even when `_lookupSubType` returns undefined (side-loaded records missing), replacing the original ids with an array of undefineds and discarding the data. The singular branch preserves the key when hydration fails; the plural branch is inconsistent and now applies to every `*_ids` attribute in REST-serializer payloads.

[Medium/test_gap] spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb — The only tests for the two new controllers assert subclass ancestry. There is no coverage of create/update/destroy happy paths, validation errors, missing records, or authorization for the new endpoints.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:~193 — `obj[k].map(...)` has no guard for a null/undefined `*_ids` value; any REST payload emitting `foo_ids: null` will throw a TypeError during hydration.

[Low/api] app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:13-15 — `update` ignores params and just re-serializes; it updates nothing. Combined with the client's `saveChanges` calling `embedding.update({})` (admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7, which is dead code — no template invokes it and it has no error handling), the PUT endpoint is a silent no-op that would discard any future embedding-level settings.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:34 — After save, the client sets `host.category` via `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`. When no category was chosen (categoryId null, e.g., new hosts), the server saves the uncategorized category but the client sets `category` to undefined, leaving the category badge blank/stale until reload.

[Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:42 — `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`; a failed DELETE leaves the row in place with no user feedback (unhandled promise rejection).

[Low/doc_defect] spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb / spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — The fabricator files were swapped: `category_fabricator.rb` now contains only the `embeddable_host` fabricator, while all the category fabricators were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. It works only because fabricators are loaded globally, but the file names no longer match their contents and will confuse maintenance.

[Low/test_gap] spec/models/topic_spec.rb:~1400 — `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer tests what its name says: the `embeddable_hosts` setting no longer exists, so the test trivially passes on the default `embed_truncate = false` and is misleading.

[Low/test_gap] test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:~227 — The `/fruits/:id` handler ignores the requested id and always returns `fruits[0]`. The updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but asserts apple's data (2 colors, ids 1–2); it passes only because of this fixture bug and would break if the handler honored `:id`.

[Low/performance] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 + app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — The allowlist check on the public `/embed/comments` endpoint now issues a DB query per request (`where("lower(host) = ?")` — non-sargable and no index exists on `host`), where the previous implementation used a cached site setting.

[Low/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The validation uses `\Z`, which matches before a trailing newline, so a host value like `"example.com\n"` passes validation and is stored with the newline (nothing strips it), after which `lower(host) = uri.host` never matches — a silently broken allowlist entry (reachable via the API; HTML inputs strip newlines).

[Low/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table ... force: true` silently drops any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table (e.g., from a partial prior run), destroying data instead of failing loudly.

[Low/test_gap] app/assets/javascripts/admin/ (components/embeddable-host.js.es6, controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6, adapters/embedding.js.es6) — The new admin embedding UI code (component save/cancel/delete flows, controller actions, adapter path) has no JavaScript tests; only the store's plural hydration path got coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration loops through `records.each do |h|` (derived from the stored `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts`) and performs `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"`. This directly interpolates `h` into SQL without quoting/escaping. A host value containing a single-quote will break the SQL, and because the value comes from the database (not validated at this point), it is an injection vector within the migration context. Using bound parameters or creating records via ActiveRecord would avoid this.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost` the validation allows a port suffix (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and the `before_validation` cleanup removes scheme and path but does not remove the port, so the DB can store `host` as e.g. `example.com:3000`. However `record_for_host` parses the URL and compares using `uri.host`, which excludes the port, so it will query for `example.com` and never match the stored `example.com:3000`. This makes such entries ineffective for `host_allowed?` checks (used in `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` / `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:~194-199 — The new plural branch unconditionally does `obj[pluralize(subType)] = hydrated; delete obj[k];` even when `_lookupSubType` returns undefined (side-loaded records missing), replacing the original ids with an array of undefineds and discarding the data. The singular branch preserves the key when hydration fails; the plural branch is inconsistent and now applies to every `*_ids` attribute in REST-serializer payloads.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new `*_ids` handling (`const m = /(.+)\_id(s?)$/.exec(k);`) maps each id through `_lookupSubType` and then **always** assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []` and **always** `delete obj[k]` (the original `*_ids` key). Since `Array#map` returns an array even when lookups fail, `hydrated` will be an array containing `undefined` entries (not falsy), and the original ids are discarded. This is inconsistent with the singular branch, which only deletes the `*_id` key when hydration succeeds, and it can cause data loss / broken behavior when sideloaded records are missing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb — The only tests for the two new controllers assert subclass ancestry. There is no coverage of create/update/destroy happy paths, validation errors, missing records, or authorization for the new endpoints.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff adds two new controllers with nontrivial behavior/endpoints:
- `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` implements `create`, `update`, and `destroy` with parameter handling and persistence (`save_host`, `destroy`) in `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`.
- `Admin::EmbeddingController` implements `show` and `update` and constructs an embedding model (`fetch_embedding`) in `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`.
However, the newly added specs `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` each only assert the controller is a subclass of `Admin::AdminController` and do not test request behavior (success cases, invalid params/validation errors, missing records in `update/destroy`, or access control/constraints). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:~193 — `obj[k].map(...)` has no guard for a null/undefined `*_ids` value; any REST payload emitting `foo_ids: null` will throw a TypeError during hydration.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6`, the new plural hydration branch (`if (m[2])`) assumes `obj[k]` is an array and immediately calls `obj[k].map(...)`. If a REST payload includes a `*_ids` key with a `null`/`undefined` value (or any non-array), this will raise a `TypeError` during `_hydrateEmbedded`. There is no guard or defaulting before calling `.map`, unlike the singular branch which passes the value through `_lookupSubType` without requiring array methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/api] app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:13-15 — `update` ignores params and just re-serializes; it updates nothing. Combined with the client's `saveChanges` calling `embedding.update({})` (admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7, which is dead code — no template invokes it and it has no error handling), the PUT endpoint is a silent no-op that would discard any future embedding-level settings.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)` without reading or persisting any params (new file `app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, update method). The client controller includes an action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({});` (`admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`), and the added template `admin/templates/embedding.hbs` does not invoke `saveChanges` (only `addHost`/`deleteHost` are wired), making it effectively unused right now. However, this is not a user-facing correctness defect in the current diff because embedding-level settings are not introduced/edited anywhere here; it’s more an incomplete/misleading PUT endpoint and dead client action that could matter if embedding-level settings are later added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:34 — After save, the client sets `host.category` via `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`. When no category was chosen (categoryId null, e.g., new hosts), the server saves the uncategorized category but the client sets `category` to undefined, leaving the category badge blank/stale until reload.

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6` `categoryId` defaults to `null` for new hosts and `save()` sends `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` (null). The server normalizes blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id` in `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, but on success the client does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));`. When `categoryId` is null, this sets `host.category` to `undefined`, so `{{category-badge host.category}}` will be blank/stale until a reload or until category is rehydrated another way. The defect is directly visible from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:42 — `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch`; a failed DELETE leaves the row in place with no user feedback (unhandled promise rejection).

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` without any `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()` which does `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE request fails, the rejection is unhandled and the UI provides no error feedback; the row also won’t be removed because `deleteHost` is only sent in the success path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/models/topic_spec.rb:~1400 — `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer tests what its name says: the `embeddable_hosts` setting no longer exists, so the test trivially passes on the default `embed_truncate = false` and is misleading.

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` under `describe "expandable_first_post?"`, the example `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets/clears any `embeddable_hosts` setting (that setting was removed from `config/site_settings.yml` and `SiteSetting`), and it also doesn't enable `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` or stub `has_topic_embed?`. Given the method now is `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (see `app/models/topic.rb`), this test will return false trivially on defaults (e.g., `embed_truncate` default false) and/or because `has_topic_embed?` is false, so the test name is misleading and not testing what it claims.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6:~227 — The `/fruits/:id` handler ignores the requested id and always returns `fruits[0]`. The updated store test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` but asserts apple's data (2 colors, ids 1–2); it passes only because of this fixture bug and would break if the handler honored `:id`.

adjudication.rationale: In `test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6`, the `this.get('/fruits/:id', ...)` handler still hardcodes `const fruit = fruits[0];`, ignoring `:id`. Meanwhile the updated test `store.find('fruit', 2)` asserts a fruit with 2 colors `[1,2]`, which matches `fruits[0]` (apple) rather than `fruits[1]` (banana has `color_ids: [3]`). The test can pass only because the pretender fixture returns the wrong fruit for id=2; it would fail if the handler respected the requested id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16 + app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:61 — The allowlist check on the public `/embed/comments` endpoint now issues a DB query per request (`where("lower(host) = ?")` — non-sargable and no index exists on `host`), where the previous implementation used a cached site setting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` to call `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?(request.referer)` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb), which in turn calls `record_for_host` and performs `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb). That is a DB query on each request to the public `/embed/comments` endpoint. The migration creating `embeddable_hosts` adds no index on `host` (db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb), and `lower(host)` would not use a normal index anyway, so this is a concrete performance concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/embeddable_host.rb:2 — The validation uses `\Z`, which matches before a trailing newline, so a host value like `"example.com\n"` passes validation and is stored with the newline (nothing strips it), after which `lower(host) = uri.host` never matches — a silently broken allowlist entry (reachable via the API; HTML inputs strip newlines).

adjudication.rationale: In app/models/embeddable_host.rb the host format validation ends with `\Z` (`/\A...\Z/i`), which in Ruby can match before a trailing newline. The `before_validation` block strips scheme and path but does not strip whitespace/newlines, so a value like `"example.com\n"` can pass validation and be persisted with the newline. Later, allowlisting uses `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` in `record_for_host`, which would not match a stored `"example.com\n"` against `uri.host` (`"example.com"`), making the entry silently ineffective (and the API controllers accept raw params into `host.host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3 — `create_table ... force: true` silently drops any pre-existing `embeddable_hosts` table (e.g., from a partial prior run), destroying data instead of failing loudly.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` explicitly uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop an existing `embeddable_hosts` table before recreating it. If the migration is re-run in a state where the table already exists (e.g., a prior failed/partial run that created the table but didn’t record the migration as applied), this can silently destroy any data already in that table instead of failing loudly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] app/assets/javascripts/admin/ (components/embeddable-host.js.es6, controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6, adapters/embedding.js.es6) — The new admin embedding UI code (component save/cancel/delete flows, controller actions, adapter path) has no JavaScript tests; only the store's plural hydration path got coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new Ember admin UI/client logic for embedding (new adapter `admin/adapters/embedding.js.es6` with `pathFor()`, controller `admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6` actions `saveChanges/addHost/deleteHost`, and component `admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6` implementing edit/save/cancel/delete flows, buffering, and focus behavior). In the test changes shown, only `test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6` and its pretender fixtures are updated to cover plural `_ids` hydration; there are no new JavaScript/acceptance/component tests exercising the new admin embedding UI behaviors or adapter path. This is a specific, diff-grounded gap rather than a runtime defect.
